rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset
rec.origin: hip_bone_l: pubic body/inferior ramus
rec.insertion: femur_l: linea aspera (proximal third)

compartments.function: Lies deep to (behind) pectineus and adductor longus, sandwiched between the anterior and posterior branches of the obturator nerve, which it is classically used to separate surgically.

zones.method: cadaveric dissection motor-point mapping, 19 limbs from 10 adult cadavers
zones.notes: Motor point measured at 21.0% +/- 4.8% (mean +/- SD, expressed here as a range) along the pubic-tubercle-to-medial-epicondyle line. zones.source: Kwon JY, Kim JS, Lee WI (2009) Am J Phys Med Rehabil 88(4):336-341, doi:10.1097/PHM.0b013e3181619435 -- retrieved via PubMed

rec.name: Biceps femoris
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset
rec.origin: hip_bone_l: long head: ischial tuberosity, inferomedial facet of the upper area (with semitendinosus, via conjoint tendon); short head: linea aspera of femur (femur_l)
rec.insertion: fibula_l: fibular head

compartments.function: Crosses both hip and knee; extends hip in addition to flexing knee.

zones.from: the superior medial aspect of the ischial tuberosity
zones.to: the proximal aspect of the medial femoral epicondyle
zones.method: cadaveric dissection to the proximal and distal limit points of the terminal intramuscular nerve endings
zones.notes: The long head's arborisation, measured on a line that runs PROXIMAL to DISTAL -- the opposite direction to the hamstring line used by Rha and by the entries on semitendinosus and semimembranosus, so the two are not directly comparable without inverting one. The motor entry point itself, where the branch first pierces the belly, is at 41.5% on this line (and 36.3% on the source's perpendicular axis from the tuberosity toward the greater trochanter), near the proximal limit of the arborised field.
zones.source: An XC, Lee JH, Im S, Lee MS, Hwang K, Kim HW, Han SH, 'Anatomic localization of motor entry points and intramuscular nerve endings in the hamstring muscles', Surg Radiol Anat 32(6):529-537 (2010), doi:10.1007/s00276-009-0609-5 -- 50 cadaveric lower extremities. Retrieved via PubMed.

zones.from: the medial and lateral TIBIAL condyles
zones.method: modified Sihler stain intramuscular arborisation mapping
zones.notes: Proximal of the two bands this source reports for biceps femoris as a whole; it does not separate the heads. On this DISTAL-to-PROXIMAL line, 50-60% is 40-50% of the way down from the tuberosity, which falls inside the long head's arborised field as measured independently by An et al. (39.7-72.9% from the tuberosity). Two studies, opposite reference directions, agreeing.
zones.source: Rha DW, Yi KH, Park ES, Park C, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular nerve distribution of the hamstring muscles: Application to treating spasticity', Clin Anat 29(6):746-751 (2016), doi:10.1002/ca.22735 -- 10 specimens per muscle, modified Sihler method. Retrieved via PubMed.

zones.from: the medial and lateral TIBIAL condyles
zones.method: modified Sihler stain intramuscular arborisation mapping
zones.notes: Distal of the two bands, equivalent to 70-85% of the way down from the ischial tuberosity. It lies in the distal third of the thigh, where the two heads are fused and a needle cannot be assigned to one head by position alone -- An et al. put the short head's field at 58.9-80.2% and the long head's at 39.7-72.9% from the tuberosity, which overlap here.
zones.source: Rha DW, Yi KH, Park ES, Park C, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular nerve distribution of the hamstring muscles: Application to treating spasticity', Clin Anat 29(6):746-751 (2016), doi:10.1002/ca.22735 -- 10 specimens per muscle, modified Sihler method. Retrieved via PubMed.

compartments.branch: common fibular (peroneal) division of sciatic n.
compartments.function: Crosses only the knee; textbook example of a single named muscle with heads innervated by different divisions of the parent nerve (tibial vs common fibular) and different actions (no hip extension).

zones.from: the superior medial aspect of the ischial tuberosity
zones.to: the proximal aspect of the medial femoral epicondyle
zones.method: cadaveric dissection to the proximal and distal limit points of the terminal intramuscular nerve endings
zones.notes: The short head's arborisation sits distal to the long head's on the same line (39.7-72.9%), which matches its more distal origin on the linea aspera. Motor entry point at 56.2% (59.7% on the source's perpendicular axis), just proximal to the field. The short head answers to the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve and the long head to the tibial division, so separating them matters for a nerve block as well as for a needle.

rec.name: Trapezius
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Johnson G, Bogduk N, Nowitzke A, House D (1994) Clin Biomech 9(1):44-50 -- dissection/volumetric study of trapezius's 3 fiber regions; the paper's own finding is more nuanced than the popular textbook summary -- it explicitly argues the essentially transverse orientation of the upper and middle fibers 'precludes any action as elevators of the scapula as commonly depicted,' proposing instead a coupled mechanism where the lower fibers fix the scapula's medial border isometrically so serratus anterior can rotate it, with upper fibers contributing to rotation only once it is already underway. The simple 'upper=elevator/middle=retractor/lower=depressor, upper+lower=force couple' model is standard simplified teaching (Gray's/Kenhub level), not this paper's own conclusion (corrected from an earlier draft that attributed the simplified model directly to this paper -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md)
rec.origin: occipital: external occipital protuberance, nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7-T12
rec.insertion: scapula_r: spine of scapula, acromion, lateral clavicle

compartments.function: Fibers run inferolaterally from occiput/upper cervical spine to the lateral clavicle/acromion; classically described as elevating the scapula, though Johnson et al.'s dissection study argues this transverse-ish fiber orientation contributes to scapular rotation mainly once rotation (driven by lower trapezius + serratus anterior) is already underway, rather than acting as a simple independent elevator.

zones.method: modified Sihler staining, whole-mount nerve arborization mapping
zones.notes: Vertical position along the occiput-to-T12 origin line. The same study also maps a horizontal (medial-to-lateral, origin-to-insertion) band at 20-40% of the muscle's width for this region -- both dimensions must be satisfied for the densest arborization, not just this vertical one. A danger zone (horizontal 40-60%, vertical 20-40%) should be avoided across all three parts: it corresponds to the accessory nerve's main trunk before it arborizes, and injecting there risks broader trapezius paralysis than intended.
zones.source: Yi KH, Lee HJ, Choi YJ, Lee K, Lee JH, Kim HJ, 'Anatomical guide for botulinum neurotoxin injection: Application to cosmetic shoulder contouring, pain syndromes, and cervical dystonia', Clin Anat 34(6):822 (2020), doi:10.1002/ca.23690 -- 16 trapezius muscles, modified Sihler's method. Retrieved via PubMed.

compartments.function: Fibers run purely transversely (horizontally) from thoracic spinous processes to the acromion/scapular spine; the muscle's pure retractor component.

zones.method: modified Sihler staining, whole-mount nerve arborization mapping
zones.notes: Vertical position along the occiput-to-T12 origin line. The horizontal (origin-to-insertion) band for this region is wider than the other two parts': 20-60% of the muscle's width. See upper trapezius's entry for the shared danger zone to avoid.
zones.source: Yi KH, Lee HJ, Choi YJ, Lee K, Lee JH, Kim HJ, 'Anatomical guide for botulinum neurotoxin injection: Application to cosmetic shoulder contouring, pain syndromes, and cervical dystonia', Clin Anat 34(6):822 (2020), doi:10.1002/ca.23690 -- 16 trapezius muscles, modified Sihler's method. Retrieved via PubMed.

compartments.function: Fibers run superolaterally from lower thoracic spinous processes to the medial scapular spine; the standard teaching model describes this depressing the scapula and, paired with the upper part, forming a force couple producing upward rotation -- though per Johnson et al.'s dissection findings, the more precise mechanism is that the lower fibers isometrically fix the scapula's medial border so serratus anterior can drive the actual rotation. Either way, a genuine 3-way fiber-direction functional split within one named muscle.

zones.method: modified Sihler staining, whole-mount nerve arborization mapping
zones.notes: Vertical position along the occiput-to-T12 origin line. The horizontal (origin-to-insertion) band for this region is 20-40% of the muscle's width, same as upper trapezius. See upper trapezius's entry for the shared danger zone to avoid.

rec.name: Anterior scalene
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.origin: cervical_vertebrae: anterior tubercles of transverse processes C3-C6
rec.insertion: ribs_r: scalene tubercle on the 1st rib

compartments.function: Forms the anterior boundary of the scalene triangle (with scalenus medius and the 1st rib) through which the brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass; the subclavian vein passes anterior to it. A classic thoracic-outlet-syndrome landmark.

zones.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology
zones.notes: INDR1. The single nerve-dense region, about 1.55 cm2, formed where the C5 branch arborises in mid-belly. longitudinal: lowest point of the jugular notch
points.path: Two finger-breadths above the clavicle, entered lateral to medial through skin, subcutaneous fat, platysma and sternocleidomastoid, aimed into the interval between the phrenic nerve and the lateral side of the ascending cervical artery, above the transverse cervical artery.

rec.name: Brachiocephalic (innominate) vein, right
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Short and nearly vertical, which is why right-sided central venous access offers the straighter path into the SVC and is generally preferred.
supplies: right internal jugular and subclavian venous return

rec.name: Superior vena cava
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Formed behind the right first costal cartilage by the union of the two brachiocephalic veins. Obstruction produces SVC syndrome -- facial and upper limb swelling, distended neck veins, collateral chest wall veins -- most often from bronchogenic carcinoma or indwelling catheter thrombus.
supplies: venous return from the head, neck, upper limbs and thoracic wall

rec.name: Inferior vena cava
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Formed by the union of the two common iliac veins at L5; drains into the right atrium. Hepatic veins (draining the liver directly into the IVC just below the diaphragm) are visceral detail outside NMSK scope.

rec.name: Common iliac artery (left)
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Mirror of the right; continues as external_iliac_a_l and internal_iliac_a_l.

rec.name: Common iliac artery (right)
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Terminal bifurcation of the aorta at L4; continues as external_iliac_a_r (modeled as the root of data/vascular/lower_limb_arterial.json) and internal_iliac_a_r.

rec.name: Common iliac vein (left)
rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Longer than the right and crosses the midline to reach the IVC, passing beneath the right common iliac artery -- the anatomical basis of May-Thurner compression syndrome.

rec.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
rec.notes: Formed by union of external_iliac_v_r (modeled as the root of data/vascular/lower_limb_venous.json) and internal_iliac_v_r.
